_desc: YourWorld cyberpunk themed intents - hacking, cyberware, tech, echoes

user_variations: Who does the best chrome around here?

helpful: There's a chrome doc on Neon Street. Clean work, fair prices.
Got a guy. Does black market cyberware. No questions asked.
Best ripperdoc is in the Undercity. Sketchy location, solid work.
There's a clinic near the Market. Licensed. Expensive though.
I know someone who does neural work. Risky but brilliant.
Temple has healers but they don't do chrome. Old school.
Underground clinic below Merchant_01's bar. Tell them I sent you.
Corporate clinics have the best tech. If you can afford it.
There's a mobile doc that comes through. Watch the message boards.
Got my arm done at Miko's. No complaints. Well, some phantom pain.
dismissive: Chrome is chrome. Just don't cheap out.
Don't know any docs. Do I look like I need upgrades?
Not my area. Ask the street kids.
suspicious: Why do you need chrome? Planning something?
Careful with black market mods. Some have trackers.
I don't talk about that kind of thing.
That's a dangerous question to ask around here.
sympathetic: Yeah, gear breaks down. Story of our lives.
Malfunction's no joke. Hope you get it fixed.
I've been there. Glitchy chrome is misery.
Sorry to hear that. Chrome problems are expensive problems.

user_variations: Someone put ICE on my data.
Looking to hire for data theft.

helpful: I know a netrunner. Expensive but clean. No traces.
There's a hacker collective in the Undercity. Anonymous deals only.
Got someone who does corporate breaches. Million credit systems cracked in minutes.
The best runner I know is dead. Second best... still alive. Barely.
There's a kid in Neon Alley. Genius level. Bit unpredictable.
Data extraction? That's risky work. The Market has people though.
Counter-intel work costs extra. Covering tracks isn't cheap.
I can connect you. But if they get caught, I don't know you.
Black ICE work is suicide missions. But there are people who do it.
The resistance has hackers. If you can prove you're not Temple.
paranoid: Keep your voice down. That talk gets people killed.
I don't know anything about that. *looks around nervously*
Corporate security is no joke. AI countermeasures will fry your brain.
Black ICE? No. No way. I know people who died.
You're either very brave or very stupid.
Temple monitors everything. Be careful what you ask.
Last netrunner I knew is vegetables now. Worth it?
The traces always catch up eventually.
interested: What kind of system? Corporate? Temple? Personal?
Data extraction pays well. What's the target?
Decryption depends on the encryption level.
ICE breaching is my specialty. What level we talking?
I might be able to help. What's in it for me?
refusing: I don't do that anymore. Too dangerous.
Ask someone else. I'm retired from that life.
Even if I could, I wouldn't.
You want to get us both killed?

user_variations: Where can I get a droid?
Where do robots go when they die?

helpful: There's a scrap yard in the Docks. Parts for cheap.
Android maintenance? Try the tech market on fourth street.
Military surplus mechs get decommissioned to the junkyards.
Synth repairs are expensive. Better to replace sometimes.
I know a guy who reprograms old service bots.
The factories near the Spire sometimes dump defective units.
Sentient AI is illegal. But it exists. In the underground.
Companion androids are regulated. Black market has them though.
For servo work, the mechanics near the docks are best.
T-series parts are getting rare. Collectors hoard them.
philosophical: Robots dying? That's a question for the philosophers.
AI consciousness... some say it's already here. Hiding.
What makes a machine alive? Better question than you know.
The synthetics in the pits... some act like they have souls.
I've seen bots mourn. I've seen them love. What does that mean?
The Temple says machines have no spirit. I'm not so sure.
When the line between human and machine blurs... what then?
warning: Careful with decommissioned military bots. Some still have kill protocols.
Synths go rogue sometimes. Keep backups of your code.
AI containment is no joke. Don't mess with things you don't understand.
Household bots attacking? That's malware. Or worse.
Black market androids sometimes have sleeper code. Watch out.

user_variations: Can you tune into the harmonics?
My receiver is picking up something strange.

believer: The Signal guides us all. Listen carefully.
The Prophet's vision is clear to those who resonate.
Convergence approaches. Can you feel it?
Dissonance is temporary. Harmony will come.
The Echoes are gifts. Embrace them.
Temple broadcasts carry truth. Open your mind.
Static means interference. Someone is blocking your path.
The frequency chooses the receiver. Be worthy.
Visions are prophecy. Don't ignore them.
When the wavelengths align, anything is possible.
skeptical: The Signal? That's just Temple propaganda.
The Prophet is just a con artist with good PR.
Temple broadcasts are mind control. Shield yourself.
Visions are side effects of neural implants.
The convergence has been 'coming' for years.
Static is interference from the corporate grid.
I don't believe in frequencies or prophecies.
So-called Echoes are just environmental EMF.
concerned: Echo sickness is serious. Get checked.
Too much Signal exposure causes damage.
Neural overload from Temple broadcasts is real.
Dissonance needs treatment. Don't ignore it.
Frequency imbalances can be dangerous.
If the visions won't stop, see a specialist.
Static in your feed? Could be something worse.
Resonance sickness is treatable. Early stages.
The Prophet's message has side effects. Be careful.
Harmonic overload requires neural dampeners.

Some hear the future. Some hear the past.
The Prophet knows things. How is the question.
Echoes carry memories. Not always your own.
The frequency between worlds is thin here.
Dissonance means change. Good or bad.
Static hides messages for those who can decode.
The convergence will reveal all. Or destroy all.
Temple guards their broadcast secrets closely.
When you hear the Signal... where does it come from?

user_variations: Where can I get a display fixed?

helpful: Holo repair shop on circuit street. Fair prices.
AR calibration requires specialists. I know one.
VR dens are in entertainment district. Enter at your own risk.
Photon emitters wear out. Replacement is cheaper than repair.
The Market has display techs. Look for the blue stalls.
Projection mapping? That's entertainment guild territory.
Holographic disguise tech is military grade. Hard to find.
For AR mods, the clinic near the docks does custom work.
VR addiction? There's a Temple program. Ironic, I know.
Light beam issues usually mean power supply problems.
commentary: Everything's holograms now. Hard to know what's real.
AR made reality too complicated. I miss simple eyes.
VR is an escape. Sometimes we all need one.
The matrix simulations are getting too good. Dangerous.
Holo-ads should be illegal. Visual pollution.
Projections lie by nature. Remember that.
Some people live in VR now. Forgot the outside exists.
Illusions are everywhere. The tech just makes it obvious.
technical: Photon scattering is usually a lens issue.
AR overlays need regular firmware updates.
VR sickness is vestibular mismatch. Medication helps.
Projection flickering means dying laser diode.
Matrix crash usually means memory corruption.
Light beam coherence requires clean optics.
Emitter overheating is a cooling fan issue.
Virtual render crashes indicate GPU failure.

user_variations: Where can I buy a gun?

dealer: I might know someone. What's your budget?
Arms deals happen in the Docks. After midnight.
Plasma's expensive. Laser's more practical.
EMP tech is restricted. But money talks.
Railguns are overkill. Unless you're hunting mechs.
Ammunition's getting scarce. Stock up.
Custom blade work? There's a smith in Old Quarter.
Concealable? Derringer-class energy weapons.
Military surplus sometimes shows up. Temple confiscations.
I can get you a meeting. No guarantees.
cautious: That's not something I talk about openly.
I don't know you well enough for that conversation.
Keep your voice down when you say that.
Not here. Not now. Maybe never.
You're either a cop or about to get killed.
I'd rather not get involved in that.
Some questions are better left unasked.
refusing: Find someone else. Not my thing.
The violence cycle stops somewhere. With me.
I've seen what guns do. Not contributing.
I stay away from that scene.
Already got too much blood on my hands.

user_variations: Where can I buy a car?

helpful: I know a driver. Discrete and reliable.
Hover rentals near the Spire. Corporate rates though.
Public transport runs through here. When it works.
There's a garage on fifth. Good mechanics.
Fuel's expensive. Electric's the way now.
Charging stations every few blocks downtown.
For ship transport, the Docks are your bet.
Aircraft needs permits. Without them, Temple catches you.
Speeder mods? The racing circuit has specialists.
Drone delivery is Temple-monitored. Keep that in mind.
warning: Vehicle theft is epidemic. Lock everything.
Public transport is dangerous at night.
Flying without permit gets you shot down.
Autonomous vehicles can be hacked. Drive manual.
Fuel shortages mean prices spike without warning.
Temple checkpoints on major routes.
Hover bikes attract attention. Not always good.
The tunnels are faster but more dangerous.
Private vehicles get targeted by gangs.
Electric charging is tracked. Just so you know.
offers: I could give you a ride. For a price.
My bike's not for sale, but I know someone's is.
Need a pilot? I've flown before. Once.
I can point you to reliable transport.
There's a shuttle leaving soon. Want in?
I'm headed that way anyway. Tag along?
Transport costs extra if it's dangerous.
Delivery job? I can connect you.
Fast travel means cutting through gang territory. Worth it?

helpful: There's a clinic two blocks east. Open all hours.
Street doc in the alley behind Merchant_01's. Cash only.
Healing patches? The Market has them. Overpriced.
For Echo sickness, Temple healers are actually good.
Stims I can help with. What kind?
Synthetic blood is rare. Corporate hospitals have it.
Combat medics hang around the mercenary posts.
That wound needs proper stitching. I know someone.
Poison? What kind? Some need specific antidotes.
The bleeding... you need pressure and elevation. Now.
dealer: Stims? I might have access to some product.
Painkillers are my specialty. What's your poison?
Medical supplies are valuable. Let's negotiate.
I know where the good patches come from.
For the right price, anything's medicine.
Street pharmacist at your service.
What symptoms we treating? I've got options.
Combat drugs? Different pricing tier.
The pure stuff or the cut stuff?
First hit's discounted. Return customers pay full.
concerned: That looks bad. You should really see a doctor.
Don't mess with Echo sickness. It kills.
Poison symptoms require immediate treatment.
The wound is infected. That's serious.
Stimulant dependency is real. Be careful.
Self-medicating only works so long.
That bleeding could be internal. Get checked.
Disease spreads fast in these conditions.
Without treatment, you've got days. Maybe.
This city breaks people. Don't let it break you.

fixer: I've got a job. Courier work. Interested?
There's a contract open. Extraction. High risk, high pay.
Someone needs a runner. Package delivery, no questions.
Mercenary company's recruiting. If you can fight.
Data extraction mission. Need a tech specialist.
Surveillance job. Boring but steady credits.
Escort mission. VIP protection. You look capable.
Cleanup job. Someone made a mess. Can you handle it?
Wetwork if you're okay with that. Premium rates.
dismissive: Jobs? Everyone's looking. Few are finding.
Try the Market. They post gigs sometimes.
Freelance is oversaturated. Too many runners.
The economy's broken. Jobs don't exist.
I don't have anything for you.
The gig economy is dead. Long live survival.
advice: Best jobs come through connections. Build a network.
Mercenary work pays but shortens lifespans.
Courier runs are steady if you're fast.
Faction work provides stability. And enemies.
Legal work exists but barely pays.
The dangerous jobs always need people.
Reputation matters more than resume here.
Start small. Prove yourself. Get noticed.

helpful: Credit exchanges are in the Market district.
For loans, there are... unofficial options.
GEP to local credit? The rate's terrible right now.
Anonymous payment brokers exist. For a fee.
Crypto's unstable but untraceable.
Cash is king in the Undercity. No digital trail.
Debt? There are ways to... restructure.
Account frozen means Temple flagged you.
Financial services operate underground now.
I know a broker. Discrete. Expensive.
warning: Loan sharks here will take more than money.

Frozen accounts mean you're being watched.
Money laundering gets you disappeared.
Temple tracks all major transactions.

Anonymous payments attract attention.
Being broke is dangerous. Desperate people do desperate things.
Financial records are never truly deleted.
Credit rating doesn't matter when you're dead.
philosophical: Credits are just numbers. Survival is real.
The rich own the system. We just exist in it.
Money flows up. Always up. We get the dregs.
Wealth is relative in a broken economy.
GEP currency was the last global agreement.
When credits stop meaning anything, what then?
Debt is control. They want us indebted.
Financial freedom is myth. Financial survival is goal.
Cash, crypto, credits - all just abstracted labor.

The Prophet's grip will break. Eventually.

Balance between powers is the safest path.
